question.en: Discuss the role of the International Development Association (IDA) in promoting inclusive growth in low-income countries.

structure.en: Introduction: Define IDA and its mandate.

introduction.en: The International Development Association (IDA), established in 1960, is the part of the World Bank that helps the world's poorest countries. It provides interest-free loans and grants to boost economic growth and reduce inequalities.
introduction.hi: The International Development Association (IDA), established in 1960, is the part of the World Bank that helps the world's poorest countries. It provides interest-free loans and grants to boost economic growth and reduce inequalities.

body.en: IDA plays a pivotal role by providing long-term financing for projects that commercial banks avoid. It focuses on human capital development (health and education), infrastructure, and climate resilience. By supporting fragile and conflict-affected states, IDA helps stabilize economies and prevent humanitarian crises. Its replenishment model ensures a steady flow of resources based on global solidarity.

conclusion.en: By bridging the financing gap for the most vulnerable nations, IDA remains a cornerstone of international development efforts, essential for achieving the 2030 Agenda.

valueAddition.en: IDA is the largest source of concessional finance for the world's 75 poorest countries.
